definitions.gloss: to be utterly dumbfounded; to be completely appalled; to be beyond amazed
definitions.explanation: An intensified form of {呆|あき}れる expressing extreme exasperation or disbelief at someone's behavior or a situation. Conveys that one has reached the absolute limit of astonishment or disgust.

examples.japanese: ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{呆|あき}れ{果|は}てた。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言|い}い{訳|わけ}→言い訳：04653_iiwake⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{呆|あき}れ{果|は}てた。
examples.english: I was completely dumbfounded by his excuses.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{直|なお}らない→直る：00735_naoru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{呆|あき}れ{果|は}てて⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{言|い}えなかった→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: No matter how many times I warned them they wouldn't change, so I was so appalled I couldn't say anything.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{呆|あき}れる→呆れる：06720_akireru⟧ (to be amazed/appalled) + ⟦{果|は}てる→果てる：28565_hateru⟧ (to reach an extreme, used as an auxiliary verb indicating completion or exhaustion). The ⟦{果|は}てる→果てる：28565_hateru⟧ suffix intensifies the meaning, expressing that one's astonishment has reached its absolute limit.

USAGE:
Almost always used in negative contexts — expressing disgust, exasperation, or disbelief at someone's foolishness, rudeness, or incompetence. Stronger than ⟦{呆|あき}れる→呆れる：06720_akireru⟧ alone. Often used in the past tense ({呆|あき}れ{果|は}てた) or て-form ({呆|あき}れ{果|は}てて).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {呆|あき}れ{果|は}てた⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧ — a look of utter disbelief
- {呆|あき}れ{果|は}てて⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{言|い}えない→言う：00515_iu⟧ — so appalled one is speechless
- ⟦すっかり→すっかり：01270_sukkari⟧{呆|あき}れ{果|は}てる — to be completely and utterly dumbfounded

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{呆|あき}れる→呆れる：06720_akireru⟧ — to be amazed, appalled (base form, less intense)
- ⟦{唖然|あぜん}→唖然：09404_azen⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to be struck dumb, speechless (focuses on being rendered speechless)
- ⟦{愕然|がくぜん}→愕然：08682_gakuzen⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to be shocked, stunned (stronger shock, can be positive or negative)
